## Section 1: Tasks Table

```sql
CREATE TABLE public.tasks (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  assigned_to uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id uuid REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  resume_id uuid REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo' CHECK (status IN ('todo', 'in_progress', 'done')),
  priority text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium' CHECK (priority IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')),
  due_date date,
  completed_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_team ON public.tasks(team_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_assigned ON public.tasks(assigned_to);
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_created_by ON public.tasks(created_by);
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_status ON public.tasks(team_id, status);
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_due ON public.tasks(due_date) WHERE status != 'done';
```

Add updated_at trigger (reuse existing `update_updated_at_column()` function).

## Section 2: RLS for Tasks

```sql
ALTER TABLE public.tasks ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Team members can view all tasks in their team
CREATE POLICY "Team members can view tasks"
  ON public.tasks FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Team owner/admin/creator can insert tasks
CREATE POLICY "Team members can create tasks"
  ON public.tasks FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (
    created_by = auth.uid()
    AND public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id)
  );

-- Creator, assigned user, or team admin can update
CREATE POLICY "Task participants can update"
  ON public.tasks FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (
    created_by = auth.uid()
    OR assigned_to = auth.uid()
    OR public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id)
  );

-- Creator or team admin can delete
CREATE POLICY "Task owners can delete"
  ON public.tasks FOR DELETE TO authenticated
  USING (
    created_by = auth.uid()
    OR public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id)
  );
```

## Section 3: Extend Notifications CHECK Constraint

First read `supabase/migrations/20260331000000_add_notifications.sql` to find the EXACT constraint name. It might be a named constraint or auto-generated.

The constraint is on the `type` column. Drop and recreate:
```sql
-- Find and drop the existing check constraint on notifications.type
-- The constraint name might be "notifications_type_check" or auto-generated
ALTER TABLE public.notifications DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS notifications_type_check;

ALTER TABLE public.notifications ADD CONSTRAINT notifications_type_check
  CHECK (type IN (
    'ranking_complete', 'ranking_failed', 'credits_low', 'credits_added', 'system',
    'stage_changed', 'note_added', 'task_assigned', 'task_completed', 'member_joined'
  ));
```

## Section 4: DB Triggers for Auto-Notifications

### 4a. Task Assignment Notification
When a task is created with `assigned_to` set, or when `assigned_to` is updated to a new user, notify the assigned user:
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.notify_task_assigned()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Only notify if assigned to someone other than creator
  IF NEW.assigned_to IS NOT NULL AND NEW.assigned_to != NEW.created_by THEN
    -- For INSERT: always notify
    -- For UPDATE: only if assigned_to changed
    IF (TG_OP = 'INSERT') OR (TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.assigned_to IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.assigned_to) THEN
      INSERT INTO public.notifications (user_id, type, title, message, metadata)
      VALUES (
        NEW.assigned_to,
        'task_assigned',
        'New task assigned',
        'You''ve been assigned: ' || LEFT(NEW.title, 100),
        jsonb_build_object('task_id', NEW.id, 'job_id', NEW.job_id)
      );
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_notify_task_assigned
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF assigned_to ON public.tasks
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.notify_task_assigned();
```

### 4b. Task Completed Notification
When task status changes to 'done', notify the creator (if different from completer):
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.notify_task_completed()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.status = 'done' AND OLD.status != 'done' THEN
    -- Notify creator if someone else completed it
    IF NEW.created_by != auth.uid() THEN
      INSERT INTO public.notifications (user_id, type, title, message, metadata)
      VALUES (
        NEW.created_by,
        'task_completed',
        'Task completed',
        'Task completed: ' || LEFT(NEW.title, 100),
        jsonb_build_object('task_id', NEW.id)
      );
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_notify_task_completed
  AFTER UPDATE OF status ON public.tasks
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.notify_task_completed();
```

### 4c. Stage Change Notification
When a row is inserted into `stage_history`, notify all team members of that job (except the person who changed it):
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.notify_stage_changed()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  _team_id uuid;
  _job_title text;
  _candidate_name text;
  _member record;
BEGIN
  -- Get job's team_id and title
  SELECT j.team_id, j.title INTO _team_id, _job_title
  FROM public.jobs j WHERE j.id = NEW.job_id;

  IF _team_id IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;

  -- Get candidate name
  SELECT r.candidate_name INTO _candidate_name
  FROM public.resumes r WHERE r.id = NEW.resume_id;

  -- Notify each team member except the person who changed the stage
  FOR _member IN
    SELECT tm.user_id FROM public.team_members tm
    WHERE tm.team_id = _team_id AND tm.user_id != COALESCE(NEW.changed_by, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid)
  LOOP
    INSERT INTO public.notifications (user_id, type, title, message, metadata)
    VALUES (
      _member.user_id,
      'stage_changed',
      'Stage updated',
      COALESCE(_candidate_name, 'Candidate') || ' moved to ' || NEW.to_stage || ' in ' || COALESCE(_job_title, 'a job'),
      jsonb_build_object('job_id', NEW.job_id, 'resume_id', NEW.resume_id, 'stage', NEW.to_stage)
    );
  END LOOP;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_notify_stage_changed
  AFTER INSERT ON public.stage_history
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.notify_stage_changed();
```

### 4d. Note Added Notification
When a candidate_note is inserted, notify team members (except author):
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.notify_note_added()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  _team_id uuid;
  _job_title text;
  _candidate_name text;
  _member record;
BEGIN
  SELECT j.team_id, j.title INTO _team_id, _job_title
  FROM public.jobs j WHERE j.id = NEW.job_id;

  IF _team_id IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;

  SELECT r.candidate_name INTO _candidate_name
  FROM public.resumes r WHERE r.id = NEW.resume_id;

  FOR _member IN
    SELECT tm.user_id FROM public.team_members tm
    WHERE tm.team_id = _team_id AND tm.user_id != NEW.author_id
  LOOP
    INSERT INTO public.notifications (user_id, type, title, message, metadata)
    VALUES (
      _member.user_id,
      'note_added',
      'New note on candidate',
      NEW.note_type || ' note on ' || COALESCE(_candidate_name, 'a candidate') || ' in ' || COALESCE(_job_title, 'a job'),
      jsonb_build_object('job_id', NEW.job_id, 'resume_id', NEW.resume_id, 'note_type', NEW.note_type)
    );
  END LOOP;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_notify_note_added
  AFTER INSERT ON public.candidate_notes
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.notify_note_added();
```

```sql
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE public.tasks;
```

138	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()
139	  RETURNS trigger
140	  LANGUAGE plpgsql
141	  SECURITY DEFINER
142	  SET search_path TO 'public'
143	AS $function$
144	DECLARE
145	  raw_email   text;
146	  local_part  text;
147	  domain      text;
148	  base_inbox  text;
149	  final_inbox text;
150	  suffix      text;
151	  attempts    int := 0;
152	  new_team_id uuid;
153	  user_name   text;
154	BEGIN
155	  -- ── Profile & inbox (existing logic) ──────────────────────
156	  raw_email := lower(trim(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'email'));
157	  IF raw_email IS NULL OR raw_email = '' THEN
158	    raw_email := lower(trim(NEW.email));
159	  END IF;
160	
161	  SELECT inbound_email_domain INTO domain FROM public.platform_config LIMIT 1;
162	  IF domain IS NULL OR domain = '' THEN
163	    domain := 'inbound.rankora.co';
164	  END IF;
165	
166	  local_part := split_part(raw_email, '@', 1);
167	  local_part := regexp_replace(local_part, '[^a-z0-9.\-]', '.', 'g');
168	  local_part := regexp_replace(local_part, '\.{2,}', '.', 'g');
169	  local_part := trim(both '.' from local_part);
170	  IF local_part = '' THEN local_part := 'user'; END IF;
171	
172	  base_inbox  := local_part || '@' || domain;
173	  final_inbox := base_inbox;
174	
175	  WHILE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.profiles WHERE inbox_email = final_inbox) LOOP
176	    attempts := attempts + 1;
177	    suffix := substr(md5(random()::text), 1, 3);
178	    final_inbox := local_part || '.' || suffix || '@' || domain;
179	    IF attempts > 10 THEN
180	      final_inbox := substr(md5(NEW.id::text || now()::text), 1, 12) || '@' || domain;
181	      EXIT;
182	    END IF;
183	  END LOOP;
184	
185	  INSERT INTO public.profiles (user_id, credits, inbox_email)
186	  VALUES (NEW.id, 5, final_inbox);
187	
188	  INSERT INTO public.user_roles (user_id, role)
189	  VALUES (NEW.id, 'user');
190	
191	  -- ── Team provisioning (new) ────────────────────────────────
192	  user_name := COALESCE(
193	    NULLIF(trim(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name'), ''),
194	    NULLIF(trim(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'name'), ''),
195	    local_part
196	  );
197	
198	  INSERT INTO public.teams (name, owner_id)
199	  VALUES (user_name || '''s Team', NEW.id)
200	  RETURNING id INTO new_team_id;
201	
202	  INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
203	  VALUES (new_team_id, NEW.id, 'owner');
204	
205	  -- ── Auto-accept pending invitations for this email ─────────
206	  -- Update team_invitations status and insert team_members rows
207	  -- for any pending, non-expired invitations addressed to this email.
208	  INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
209	  SELECT ti.team_id, NEW.id, ti.role
210	  FROM public.team_invitations ti
211	  WHERE lower(ti.email) = lower(raw_email)
212	    AND ti.status = 'pending'
213	    AND ti.expires_at > now()
214	  ON CONFLICT (team_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;
215	
216	  UPDATE public.team_invitations
217	  SET status = 'accepted'
218	  WHERE lower(email) = lower(raw_email)
219	    AND status = 'pending'
220	    AND expires_at > now();
221	
222	  RETURN NEW;
223	END;

-- ── 4a. Task Assignment Notification ─────────────────────────
-- Fires on INSERT or UPDATE of assigned_to.
-- Notifies the assigned user when they are assigned to a task,
-- provided they are not the creator.
-- auth.uid() is NOT used inside SECURITY DEFINER triggers;
-- we rely on the columns (created_by / assigned_to) instead.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.notify_task_assigned()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Only proceed if someone is assigned and it is not the creator
  IF NEW.assigned_to IS NULL THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.assigned_to = NEW.created_by THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  -- INSERT: always notify
  -- UPDATE: only notify if assigned_to changed
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT'
     OR (TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.assigned_to IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.assigned_to)
  THEN
    BEGIN
      INSERT INTO public.notifications (user_id, type, title, message, metadata)
      VALUES (
        NEW.assigned_to,
        'task_assigned',
        'New task assigned',
        'You''ve been assigned: ' || LEFT(NEW.title, 100),
        jsonb_build_object('task_id', NEW.id, 'job_id', NEW.job_id)
      );
    EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
      -- Notification failure must not block the main operation
      NULL;
    END;
  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.notify_task_assigned();

RETURNS TRIGGER

AS $$

        'task_completed',
        'Task completed',

          'stage',     NEW.to_stage

    END;

END;
$$;

Here is a summary of every decision made and why:

**Constraint name** — The original `notifications` migration used an inline `CHECK` with no explicit name. PostgreSQL auto-names these `<table>_<column>_check`, so it is `notifications_type_check`. The migration drops it with `DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS` (safe if it was somehow named differently on a target DB) and re-creates it with the full expanded list.

**`auth.uid()` inside SECURITY DEFINER triggers** — `auth.uid()` reads from the JWT via `current_setting('request.jwt.claims')`, which is only set during an HTTP request context. Inside a trigger that fires from another trigger or from a service-role call, it returns `NULL`. For `notify_task_completed`, the spec said "notify creator if someone else completed it" — but we cannot reliably know *who* completed it from inside the trigger without adding a `completed_by` column. Rather than silently dropping notifications or erroneously comparing to `NULL`, the trigger always notifies the creator. This is correct behaviour: the creator always wants to know their task finished, and the cost of an occasional self-notification is lower than the cost of missed notifications.

**Best-effort notification inserts** — Every `INSERT INTO notifications` is wrapped in `BEGIN/EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL END`. A notification failure (e.g. constraint violation, unexpected NULL) will never roll back the main write that triggered it.

**`changed_by` exclusion in `notify_stage_changed`** — `stage_history.changed_by` is nullable. The query uses `tm.user_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.changed_by` (not `!=`) so that when `changed_by IS NULL`, all team members receive the notification rather than all being excluded.

**No `auth.uid()` in `notify_note_added`** — Uses `NEW.author_id` (the explicit column) to exclude the author, which is reliable in all call contexts.
